Vaibhav Jain
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Datt - Senior Advocate with Shri Rohit Sha
 Advocate for applicant.
 Shri Manoj Jha - Panel Lawyer for State.
 Shri Siddharth Bhola - Advocate for respondent No.2/co
 Order

This first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/ Section 438 of Cr.P.C for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.128/2024, registered at Police Station Kareli,
District Narsinghpur (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420, 406 and 409 of the IPC.

2. As per prosecution story, the complainant lodged an FIR against the applicant and co-accused persons alleging that the complainant had a business transaction with the applicant and co-accused and the complainant delivered grains of Rs.4,32,34,022/- from 19 of Oct. 2023 to 6 of Dec 2023.

It is also alleged that the present applicant and co-accused paid a sum of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:6161 2 MCRC-5684-2025 Rs.3,67,34,391/- and cheated the complainant by non-payment of remaining amount of Rs.64,99,531/-.
On the basis of above, aforesaid offence was registered against the present applicant and co-accused persons.
3. Learned senior counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is submitted that applicant is not the main accused.
In the written FIR, name of present applicant is not mentioned.
Main accused are Rakesh and Mukesh who have been enlarged on bail by this Court.
There has been settlement between the complainant and main accused persons alongwith the present applicant.
This is a civil dispute between the parties.
It is further submitted that major payment has already been paid by applicant.
There is no need of custodial interrogation.
In these circumstance, applicant may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for complainant submits that there has been settlement between both the parties, therefore, he has no objection in granting bail to applicant.
5. Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.
5. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the anticipatory bail application filed by the applicant is allowed.

It is directed that if the applicant is arrested by the police then he shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer/Arresting Authority.
